summary: Retest of the single open bug from iteration_4: the TOCTOU race in sync_sources() (backend/routers/tax.py) that caused intermittent 500 DuplicateKeyError on GET /api/auditpro/tax/documents and /tax/summary. Fix (atomic update_one upsert + DuplicateKeyError caught as already-synced) verified: the dedicated race-condition backend test passed 6/6 consecutive runs (previously failed most runs), and the full backend suite + all 8 existing browser checks pass with no regression. Both acceptance_matrix criteria are satisfied.

action_items.note: tests/test_tscheck_document_extraction.py, test_tscheck_document_validation.py, test_tscheck_duplicate_detection.py, and test_tscheck_assistant_proposal_flow.py (one of its two cases) intermittently fail on the LIVE Gemini OCR/LLM call with 502 'Gemini tidak dapat memproses dokumen ini' or a dropped 'proposal' SSE event, then pass cleanly on immediate rerun with no code change. Matches spec_deviations (live LLM latency/availability) - not classified as a bug, carried forward for visibility only, not part of this retest's scope.

When tests/test_tscheck_tax_sync_idempotent.py is run in a custom subset alongside other tax test files (bypassing the pinned pytest.ini -n 2 --dist loadscope module grouping that the full-suite run uses), its own fresh transaction can get swept up by a concurrent test module's global POST /tax/sync call first, making its own 'created' count 0. This only reproduces when cherry-picking files outside the configured worker/module grouping; the full `pytest tests/` run (the supported invocation) passes this test consistently across 3 repeated runs. Not a regression from the race-condition fix and not reproducible via the UI or single-file run.

checks.criterion: Tax sync is race-safe: concurrent GETs after approving a fresh expense never 500
checks.name: test_tscheck_tax_sync_race_condition.py
checks.evidence: 6 concurrent GET /api/auditpro/tax/documents immediately after approving a fresh tscheck-prefixed expense transaction. Ran the file 6 times in a row post-fix: '1 passed' every time (previously: intermittent 500 DuplicateKeyError on most runs, e.g. statuses [500,200,200,200,500,200]). No pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError observed in any of the 6 runs.
